## CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TASKS

Claude Code provides the four Task tools (TaskCreate, TaskUpdate, TaskGet, TaskList), or TodoWrite instead when you set CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TASKS=0. You can revert to the old behavior with the env var CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TASKS=false.

## TodoWrite

TodoWrite is the lightweight, original mechanism where the agent creates a checklist; items move through pending → in_progress → completed. However, as of Claude Code v2.1.16 (released January 22, 2026), TodoWrite has been superseded by the new Tasks API — TaskCreate, TaskUpdate, TaskList, and TaskGet.

## TaskCreate

TaskCreate is used for multi-step work, with dependencies set using addBlockedBy for sequential phases. When watching for TaskCreate, you watch for TaskCreate and TaskUpdate and accumulate items into a map keyed by task ID.

## Model Availability

Claude Code v2.1.233 disabled TodoWrite, TaskCreate, TaskGet, TaskUpdate, and TaskList by default on Opus 4.8, Sonnet 5, Fable 5, Mythos 5, and later models to free up context space, since newer models track multi-step work without a written checklist. # Track todos

> Track todos in Agent SDK sessions and render Claude's progress in your application from structured tool calls

Claude Code provides the [task-tracking tools](/docs/en/tools-reference#task-tool-availability) by default only on the models listed under [Model availability](#model-availability). Newer models track multi-step work without a written todo list, so on those you don't need anything on this page for Claude to work through multi-step tasks.

In a session that has the task-tracking tools, Claude keeps a written todo list, updating each item's status as it works. You see each change in the message stream as a structured tool call. Opt a session in only when your application reads those tool calls, whether to log task activity or to render its own progress display.

## Model availability

<Note>
  The following tools are available by default only on Claude 3.x models, Opus 4 through 4.7, Sonnet 4 through 4.6, and Haiku 4.5. On every other model, including model IDs Claude Code doesn't recognize, they aren't available unless you opt in:

  * `TodoWrite`
  * `TaskCreate`
  * `TaskGet`
  * `TaskUpdate`
  * `TaskList`

  Wherever the tools are available, Claude Code provides the four Task tools, or `TodoWrite` instead when you set `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TASKS=0`.

  This default set applies in Claude Code v2.1.268 and later, which the TypeScript Agent SDK bundles from v0.3.268.
</Note>

On a model that doesn't have the tools by default, unless you opt a session in, you see no `tool_use` blocks for them in the message stream. The Agent SDK applies these defaults through the Claude Code binary that it bundles. If you point `pathToClaudeCodeExecutable` (TypeScript) or `cli_path` (Python) at your own Claude Code install, you get whichever tools that install provides, under its own defaults. To see the exact set in a running session, [check which tools are available](/docs/en/tools-reference#check-which-tools-are-available). To opt a session in, do one of the following:

* Name one of the tools in the [`allowedTools`](/docs/en/agent-sdk/permissions#allow-and-deny-rules) (TypeScript) or `allowed_tools` (Python) option
* List the tools in the `tools` option, which restricts the session's built-in tools to the ones it names. Include the tools you want alongside the other built-in tools you use
* Set `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TODO_TOOLS=1` in the `env` option, as the examples on this page do. In TypeScript, `env` replaces the subprocess environment, so spread `...process.env` to keep inherited variables. In Python, `env` is merged on top of the inherited environment

## Todo lifecycle

Claude moves each todo through a predictable lifecycle:

1. **Created**: Claude adds the todo as `pending` when it identifies a task
2. **Activated**: Claude sets the todo to `in_progress` when it starts the work
3. **Completed**: Claude marks it completed when the task finishes successfully
4. **Removed**: Claude deletes a todo it no longer needs by setting `status: "deleted"` in a `TaskUpdate` call

## When Claude creates todos

In a [session that has the task-tracking tools](#model-availability), Claude creates todos for most multi-step work, such as:

* **Complex multi-step tasks** requiring three or more distinct actions
* **User-provided task lists** when multiple items are mentioned
* **Longer operations** that benefit from progress tracking
* **Explicit requests** when users ask for todo organization

Claude may skip todos for very short or single-step requests.

## Examples

Before running these examples, install the Claude Agent SDK by following the [quickstart](/docs/en/agent-sdk/quickstart). Every example on this page shares the same permission setup and exit behavior:

entries.content:
Yes, this is possible through the CLI. The tools exist in Claude Code but are switched off by default for newer models, and one environment variable turns them back on.

## Why Claude said it had no task-tracking tool

Claude Code has built-in task-tracking tools: `TaskCreate`, `TaskUpdate`, `TaskGet` and `TaskList` (the older `TodoWrite` is used instead if `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TASKS=0` is set). Since Claude Code v2.1.233 these tools are **off by default on newer models**, including Opus 4.8+, Sonnet 5 and Fable 5. Anthropic's reason is that newer models track multi-step work without a written checklist. Older models (Opus 4–4.7, Sonnet 4–4.6, Haiku 4.5) still get them by default.

You can switch them back on without changing any flags: set `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TODO_TOOLS=1` in the environment, or name one of the tools in `--allowedTools` / `--tools`.

**I checked this on your machine** (Claude Code 2.1.280, model `claude-opus-5-5`). I ran md2's one-shot command, `claude -p --verbose --output-format stream-json`, and looked at the tool list in the startup (`init`) event:
- **Without the variable:** no task tools in the list.
- **With `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TODO_TOOLS=1`:** `TaskCreate`, `TaskGet`, `TaskList` and `TaskUpdate` are all present.

## What md2 would need

1. **Enabling it is small.** `createAgentEnvironment` in `desktop/src/actions/agent/agent_environment.js` already adds one Claude-only variable (`CLAUDE_FORWARD_SUBAGENT_TEXT_VARIABLE`). The new variable would follow the same pattern. That function copies your own environment through, so setting the variable in Windows before starting md2 would work today with no code change.
2. **Open question: always on, or a setting?** Anthropic turned the tools off to save context space, so enabling them for every run costs some tokens. Choosing between always on, a per-agent-profile option, or a per-action option is your call.
3. **Showing the tasks is the bigger part.** They arrive as ordinary `TaskCreate` / `TaskUpdate` tool calls in the stream. I expect md2 would show them as generic tool entries, but I didn't check how they render. A real task list would mean pairing each `TaskCreate` with its result to get the task id, keeping the list in a service, and sending an update event for each task. That matches the event rules in AGENTS.md.

## Codex

Codex already has a plan tool (`update_plan`), so it doesn't need opting in. I believe md2 doesn't show it yet, but I haven't run Codex to confirm:
- **One-shot (`exec --json`):** Codex sends it as a `todo_list` item. Its content is in an `items` array, and `codexTranscriptContent` in `desktop/src/actions/agent/agent_codex_events.js` doesn't read that field, so it would be dropped silently.
- **Streaming (`app-server`):** Codex sends plan changes as a `turn/plan/updated` notification. `handleNotification` in `desktop/src/actions/agent/agent_streaming_adapter.js` has no case for it. The `plan` item md2 does handle there is Codex's plan-mode proposal, which is a different thing.

I haven't changed any code or the F_380 card. If you'd like, I can add these findings to the card; tell me whether to enable the variable always or behind a setting.

Sources:
- [Track todos – Claude Code Docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/todo-tracking)
- [Claude Code v2.1.233: Todo tool disabled by default – DevelopersIO](https://dev.classmethod.jp/en/articles/20260815-cc-updates-v2-1-233/)

## About your note: the special messages are tool searches

The model was checking whether a task tool exists. Three stored conversations show it calling `ToolSearch`:
- In card `6c251422…`, it searched for `"TaskCreate"` and got "No matching deferred tools found".
- In cards `06697134…` and `55646f70…`, it searched for `"task create todo"` and got only unrelated tools back (`TaskStop`, `CronCreate`, …).

Once `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TODO_TOOLS=1` is set, the task tools are in the startup tool list (I checked this last time), so these searches should stop. Today each one costs a tool call and shows up as a `tool.ToolSearch` row.

## How it works today

- **Claude:** `TaskCreate`/`TaskUpdate` calls would show as generic `tool.TaskCreate` rows containing raw JSON. They go through `claudeToolEvent` in streaming mode and `claudeTranscriptEvents` in one-shot mode.
- **Codex streaming:** `turn/plan/updated` is not handled in `handleNotification`, so it's dropped silently. I confirmed its shape from the installed CLI's own schema: `{ threadId, turnId, explanation?, plan: [{ step, status: pending|inProgress|completed }] }`.
- **Codex one-shot:** the plan arrives as a `todo_list` item. It isn't in `SUPPORTED_CODEX_ITEM_TYPES`, so it shows up as a "Codex protocol diagnostic" row. The parser also ignores `item.updated`, which is where intermediate updates of the list would arrive. I haven't verified this item's exact shape against codex 0.156; that needs a check.

## Proposed model

The desktop turns each provider's format into one provider-neutral task list, stored on the conversation. That makes it model data: it's saved with the conversation and still there after a reload.

```
conversation.taskList = { tasks: [{ id, subject, status: 'pending'|'inProgress'|'completed', activeForm? }], updatedAt }
```

Each change replaces the whole list. Codex always sends the full plan anyway, and Claude lists are small.

## Desktop

1. **Turn the tools on.** `createAgentEnvironment` in `agent_environment.js` would add `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TODO_TOOLS=1` for Claude, following the existing forward-subagent-text variable.
2. **Claude decoder.** A new class next to `ClaudeFileResultDecoder` in `agent_claude_events.js`. It must go there because that file's own comment says decoders are shared by the one-shot and streaming paths. It would:
   - Remember each `TaskCreate` by its `tool_use.id`.
   - When the tool result arrives, read the new task's id from `tool_use_result.task.id` (same pairing trick the file decoder uses).
   - Apply each `TaskUpdate` to its task. Read the id as `taskId`, `id` or `task_id`, because Claude Code repairs these key names but the stream doesn't show the repair.
   - Remove a task when its status becomes `deleted`; ignore results marked `is_error`.
3. **Codex streaming.** Handle `turn/plan/updated` in `agent_streaming_adapter.js`, root thread only.
4. **Codex one-shot.** Handle `todo_list` items on `item.started`, `item.updated` and `item.completed` in `agent_provider_protocol.js`, so they no longer become diagnostic rows.
5. **Runner.** `agent_runner_service.js` sets `run.conversation.taskList` and emits a new run event, `taskList`.
6. **Persistence.** `parseAgentConversationValue` in `shared/agent_conversations.mjs` only keeps fields it knows, so it needs a `taskList` validator. Without it the list is lost on reload.

## Communications

- `action_run.js` would forward the run event as a new update kind, `{ kind: 'agentTaskList', taskList }`, next to the existing `agentUsage`.
- No new IPC channel is needed; it uses the existing action event stream.
- Add the new update kind to the update type list in `app/src/data/action_run_types.ts`, and add `taskList` to the `AgentConversation` type.

## Renderer

- `action_run_registry.ts` applies `agentTaskList` to `conversation.taskList`, with its own change kind. That way the transcript isn't treated as changed, which keeps to the rule against republishing the whole conversation for one field.
- A new leaf component, `AgentTaskList`, renders the list:
  - It subscribes with `useSyncExternalStore` and returns `conversation.taskList` as a stable reference.
  - It's placed in the conversation chat, probably above the prompt or in the status area.
  - It shows only when the list has items, follows the `STYLE_GUIDE.md` patterns, and works for both live and historical conversations.

## Decisions for you

1. **Turning it on:** always on for Claude, or an option per agent profile? Anthropic switched the tools off to save context, so always-on costs tokens on every run.
2. **Raw rows:** hide the raw `tool.TaskCreate`/`tool.TaskUpdate` (and Codex plan) rows from the transcript once the panel exists, or keep them?
3. **Sub-agents:** Claude sub-agent events carry `parent_tool_use_id`. Should their tasks be ignored, or merged into the parent's list? I haven't confirmed whether Claude shares one task list across sub-agents.
4. **Placement:** panel above the prompt, in the status/meta area, or a collapsible section?

## Edge cases

- **Resumed sessions:** after `--resume`, Claude's own task state may differ from what md2 stored. The last stored list is shown until the next update replaces it.
- **Codex across turns:** Codex may send a fresh plan each turn, so "latest snapshot wins" fits.
- **Old conversations:** ones without `taskList` simply show no panel.

## Tests

- Unit tests for the Claude decoder, run through both the one-shot and streaming paths.
- Tests for the Codex `turn/plan/updated` and `todo_list` handling.
- Tests for the `taskList` field in `parseAgentConversationValue`.
- A registry test for the `agentTaskList` update.
- A React Testing Library test for the panel.

All of these use fixture events and don't run the CLIs.
